papers.summary: We give a direct proof of the equivalence between the Muckenhoupt $\mathcal{A}_2$ and the Helson--Szegő conditions on the unit circle $T$. A positive weight $w$ belongs to $\mathcal{A}_2(T)$ if and only if $\log w=u+Hv$, where $u,v$ are real bounded functions, $\|v\|_\infty<\fracπ{2}$, and $H$ denotes the periodic Hilbert transform. The classical proof combines the Helson--Szegő theorem with the Hunt--Muckenhoupt--Wheeden characterization of weighted boundedness of the Hilbert transform. Our proof derives the Helson--Szegő representation directly from the Muckenhoupt $\mathcal{A}_2$ condition, without using boundedness of $H$ on $L^2(w)$.
papers.title: A direct proof of the equivalence of the A2 and the Helson--Szego conditions

papers.summary: The cyclicity index is used to study the periodic behavior of powers of tropical matrices. It is determined by the structure of the critical subgraph of a matrix, which consists of the cycles with the largest average weight. In this paper bijective linear transformations of tropical matrices that preserve an individual value $k\neq 2$ of this invariant are studied.
papers.title: Linear transformations of tropical matrices preserving individual values of the cyclicity index

papers.summary: We disprove the cap-sufficiency proposal in Wright's Problem 16 for $1<p<(\sqrt{13}-1)/2$ and for $p>3$. For each fixed exponent in these ranges, one smooth strictly convex domain has finite original directional cap integral, while the lacunary maximal operator of complete arclength fails restricted weak type. We also give a geometric sufficient condition for strong $L^p$ boundedness, for every finite $1<p<\infty$, on an arbitrary given bounded convex domain. It requires one logarithmic integral of a curvature lower envelope, without a differentiability assumption on the boundary or a restriction on the number of curvature zeros. Both results concern unnormalised true arclength, one fixed interior origin and all integer dyadic dilations.
papers.title: Lacunary maximal operators on convex boundaries

papers.summary: A linear monodimensional lattice Boltzmann scheme with three velocities tackling the advection equation is investigated. We prove that it is second-order accurate and provide necessary and sufficient stability conditions through an explicit formula involving the two relaxation parameters. Relying on existing results for finite difference schemes, we prove convergence for smooth initial data with initialization of the non-conserved moments at equilibrium. Several numerical simulations illustrate these theoretical findings.
papers.title: Numerical analysis of a Lax-Wendroff type lattice Boltzmann scheme for the advection equation

papers.summary: We prove sharp bounds for the upper and lower intermediate dimensions of orthogonal and radial projections of compactly supported measures. Both dimension functions are preserved almost everywhere when the quasi-Assouad dimension does not exceed the target dimension. We obtain exceptional-set estimates using the entire source dimension function, with sharpness for explicit families. We also construct a fixed measure whose projected dimension functions vary on open direction sets, even when all source dimensions lie below the target dimension.
papers.title: Sharp Projection Bounds for Intermediate Dimensions of Measures

papers.summary: We learn schedules for a continuous penalty relaxation of MAX-CUT by backpropagating through an unrolled classical solver. A state-blind schedule generalizes to instances substantially larger than those used for training. A state-adaptive bilinear schedule also generalizes out of distribution, outperforming its untrained baseline across 15 seeds ($t=4.1$). By contrast, an additive ablation with identical inputs and output heads is statistically indistinguishable from the bilinear model in distribution but performs worse than its own baseline out of distribution ($t=-11.7$). This separation appears without regularization and persists across a $30$ round weight-decay sweep: the bilinear advantage remains significant at every tested value, whereas the additive model never recovers. The results in this setting isolate how solver state enters the schedule, rather than state adaptivity alone, as the architectural distinction associated with out-of-distribution transfer.
papers.title: Multiplicative vs. Additive State Coupling in Learned Optimizer Schedules

papers.summary: The $S$-function method for rational second order ODEs $y''=\varphi(x,y,y')$ uses $S=I_y/I_z$, attached to a first integral $I$, which satisfies a Riccati equation along the flow; it was designed for Liouvillian $I$. We study the case of rational $S$ with non-Liouvillian $I$. From any rational $g(x,y,z)$ with $g_z\neq0$ and any linear equation $A_2w''+A_1w'+A_0w=0$ with polynomial coefficients, the substitution $w'/w=g(x,y,y')$ yields a rational 2ODE whose first integral is built from two independent solutions, and $S=g_y/g_z$: the Wronskian cancels, so $S$ does not see the linear equation, and one rational $S$ is shared by equations with and without Liouvillian first integrals. Conversely, given $(\varphi,S)$, membership in this class reduces to a rational first integral of an explicit planar vector field plus a Möbius-invariant Riccati test in $x$, which recovers the linear equation. A transfer theorem shows that $I$ is Liouvillian if and only if this equation has a Liouvillian solution, so Liouvillianity is decidable on the class by Kovacic's algorithm: a three-variable problem with no a priori degree bound is reduced to two classical ones. On nine pull-back equations of degree up to $15$, given without information on their construction, the procedure recovers the Airy equation and the Bessel equation of order zero.
papers.title: Rational $S$-functions for second order ODEs with non-Liouvillian first integrals

papers.summary: We examine the use of neural networks in conjunction with the Born approximation for solving the inverse scattering problem for a penetrable medium in the frequency domain. The goal is a fast method for determining the refractive index of a scatterer from multistatic far-field measurements at one frequency. We present a new neural network model that seeks to improve on our previous results in by sharpening the reconstructed images. In addition, we present two other networks motivated by the corrected Born method that avoid the need to invert the regularized Born operator. These latter algorithms will be important for future three dimensional applications when the inverse Born approximation is difficult to compute, or when near-field measurements are used. Computational results illustrate that the new corrections to the Born approximation can provide an accurate and flexible approach to the inverse scattering problem.
papers.title: Neural network enhancement of the Born approximation

papers.summary: Simplified spectral models predict dimension-dependent superlinear convergence for gradient methods, but the corresponding behavior of actual iterations remains only partially understood. Historical methods introduce an additional difficulty: the gradients defining the step sizes differ from those receiving them. We study this offset for cyclic reuse of historical Ritz step sizes on strictly convex quadratics. Within the existing limited memory steepest descent with retards (LMSDR) family, a rolling cyclic Ritz (RCR) rule reuses $m$ historical Ritz values $\ell$ times per cycle, ending with a complete sweep. At $q=m+1$ active distinct eigenvalues, an exact delayed recurrence gives almost-everywhere doubly exponential convergence with an explicit rate and exceptional weights. Nonempty open basins also exist for $m+1<q\le2m$ and $\ell\ge4$. Rebuilding the history from each cycle-start gradient costs $m$ additional updates and gives sampled cyclic Ritz reuse (SCR) a cycle-end map determined by the current weights. Under uniform sampling bounds, SCR converges doubly exponentially almost everywhere when $(2\ell-1)^m>\binom{q-1}{m}$. Increasing $\ell$ admits larger $q$ for fixed $m$. The guarantee extends to history-dependent choices from finite sampling menus under a bound on the number of admissible sampling sequences. Geometrically spaced decisions retain the SCR condition and rate range. Every update is counted, including sampling; a numerical illustration compares finite-tolerance update counts.
papers.title: Superlinear Convergence of Cyclic Gradient Methods with Historical Ritz Step Sizes

papers.summary: We show that independent random points support exact quadrature rules with positive weights. For any $n$-dimensional space $V$ of integrable functions a constant multiple of $n\log n$ points sampled from a suitable density yields, with high probability, positive weights which integrate the functions in the space exactly. The weights stay close to the natural importance sampling weights according to the Lewis density with respect to $V$. They are the result of a weight adaptation procedure which requires an explicit $L_1$-norm discretization result that is proved on the way. As an application, we study numerical integration in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. Combining the random rules with a subsampling step, we show that positive quadrature rules with constantly oversampled nodes achieve the best possible worst-case error bound in terms of the singular numbers of the embedding into $L_2$.
papers.title: Random nodes with positive weights: Richter-Tchakaloff rules and optimal positive quadrature

papers.summary: Decoupling inequalities for the parabola are obtained for weights in physical space. The decoupling iteration relies on a fractal bilinear Kakeya estimate. We record applications to exponential sums.
papers.title: Weighted decoupling inequalities via fractal bilinear Kakeya estimates

papers.summary: For $d,n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq1}$ and $p\in[1,\infty)\setminus\{2\}$, we characterize all linear maps $s\colon\ell_d^p\to\ell_n^p$ for which there is $E\subseteq X_d$ such that $\|s(ξ)\|_p=\|ξ|_E\|_p$ for every $ξ\in\ell_d^p$. We call these maps \emph{restricted isometries}. Our Lamperti-type theorem gives a unique description of each such operator using a set transformation, a positive amplitude function, and a unimodular phase function. In particular, it includes noninjective and nonsurjective operators, even when the dimensions differ. We further characterize restricted isometries between finite $\ell^p$-spaces with arbitrary positive atomic weights. Applications include formulas counting set transformations and uniform restricted isometries, as well as a geometric description of all restricted isometries with fixed column supports.
papers.title: Restricted isometries in finite-dimensional $\ell^p$-spaces

papers.summary: A biderivation of an algebra is a bilinear map which is a derivation in each argument. We describe all biderivations of finite-dimensional complex null-filiform and filiform Zinbiel algebras. For the n-dimensional null-filiform algebra, every biderivation is determined by an arbitrary value at its generating pair; the space of biderivations has dimension n and consists entirely of symmetric maps. For the three standard filiform families, we give explicit bases and determine their symmetric and skew-symmetric parts. We also treat all filiform algebras of dimensions at most four, including the exceptional families not covered by the classification in dimensions at least five. A three-dimensional algebra admits a three-dimensional space of skew-symmetric biderivations, two of which have values outside its annihilator. Up to isomorphism, it is the unique complex filiform Zinbiel algebra with this property. The proofs use generators, annihilator-valued maps, a truncated polynomial model, and conformal endomorphisms of bilinear forms.
papers.title: Biderivations of Null-Filiform and Filiform Zinbiel Algebras

papers.summary: We give a length-two counterexample to the unrestricted product comparison in Bergman's Question 3.1, positive criteria for quasi-injective common modules, and a semidirect-product version of Question 3.2. For semiprimary right self-injective rings, the countable hull construction yields a cyclic two-layer witness, its Baer class, and an opposite-side extension obstruction. We apply this construction over the square-zero ring of the counterexample. The hull quotient of a countable sum of injectives is the endomorphism space modulo finite-rank maps, and computes the full socle-radical defect of a countable product of the regular module. This gives a second counterexample with free cyclic family factors. The original length-two product embeds its defect in the same quotient through an explicit intersection, and all associated extension classes arise from one specified Baer class. The general Faith conjecture remains unresolved.
papers.title: Finite stabilization, socle extensions, and Faith's conjecture

papers.summary: The Medvedev lattice is a tool used to classify the complexity of effective closed sets. In this article, we are interested in the complexity of using this tool. In particular, we study the complexity of deciding whether two effective closed sets have the same degree, when one is fixed and the other is given as input. This problem is naturally~$Σ^0_3$, and among other results, we show that for all degrees except the maximal one, the problem reaches its maximal complexity. It turns out that the argument is not uniform and depends on the self-similarity of the fixed degree, a notion that we introduce in this article. The complexity of having maximal degree is particularly difficult to establish, but we obtain a lower bound that almost matches the upper bound. We also show that deciding whether an effective closed set has a degree incomparable with a fixed degree $d$ is $Π^0_3$-complete whenever $\mathbf{0}_s <_s d <_s \mathbf{1}_s$.
papers.title: On the complexity of Medvedev reducibility

papers.summary: We show that random tuples of matrices over a finite field are uniform dimension expanders for every expansion coefficient below the optimal one, using elementary counting arguments. The same holds for the optimal coefficient along a set of dimensions of density 1. By contrast, along Fibonacci dimensions random pairs of matrices fail to be optimal dimension expanders with probability bounded away from zero.
papers.title: Optimality of finite field dimension expanders

papers.summary: We show that each of the infinitely many extensions of the basic inquisitive logic has the Craig interpolation property, and deduce from this that each of these extensions also has the Beth definability property. These results stand in contrast to existing characterizations of interpolation within lattices of extensions, in which the distribution of logics with interpolation is sparse.
papers.title: Interpolation in the Inquisitive Hierarchy

papers.summary: We study the structure of amenable subrelations of treeable measure-class-preserving equivalence relations, applying the Radon--Nikodym topography perspective initiated in our companion paper [TTD25]. For a nowhere smooth amenable subrelation, we show that the ends selected by each class in Adams's end selection theorem are precisely those which are nonvanishing along that class. From this, we derive a number of structure results about nowhere smooth amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations. For example, we show that every nowhere smooth amenable subrelation is contained in an essentially unique maximal amenable subrelation. This yields an anti-treeability criterion, which we use to show that every nonamenable locally compact second countable group with noncompact amenable radical is not treeable, and that every nonamenable nonunimodular treeable group has a compact open subgroup.
papers.title: Amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations and applications to anti-treeability

papers.summary: In this paper, we prove that the set of groups satisfying the minimal condition on centralizers is a complete co-analytic subset of the Polish space of countable groups. This answers a question of Wesolek and Williams.
papers.title: Groups satisfying the minimal condition on centralizers are complete co-analytic

papers.summary: A hard theorem of Givant classifies the finitary algebraic theories for which every algebra is free. From it, one easily deduces that all such theories are minimal (adding any further equations makes them trivial) and have a well-defined notion of dimension (free algebras on sets of different cardinality are never isomorphic). We prove both these properties directly, without the aid of Givant's theorem.
papers.title: Properties of theories whose algebras are free
